https://enrsi.stvr.sk/articles/news/4545.text: The Foreign Ministry condemns any attacks on civilians, civilian infrastructure or diplomatic missions anywhere in the world that are protected under international law. The Ministry issued this statement on social media in response to Friday's (24 July) Russian attack on the town of Sloviansk in Ukraine. "Slovakia has long been calling for an end to the war in Ukraine, for which there is no military solution; we therefore fully support the peace efforts, which are absolutely essential," stated the Ministry. Both Ukraine and Russia launched further attacks against each other on Friday, resulting in several casualties on both sides. Kyiv attacked the Russian city of Kirov, which is located more than 1,000 kilometres behind the front line. Moscow launched an attack on Kyiv region. The city of Sloviansk in Donetsk region was also targeted by the Russian attack, where five people were killed and the premises of the Latvian Honorary Consulate were damaged. Source: TASR

https://telex.hu/sport/2026/09/26/toth-b.text: Menü Kereső Tóth Balázs: Nagyon csalódottak vagyunk, mert többet érdemeltünk volna Sport Klág Dávid Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom „Nagyon csalódottak vagyunk, mert többet érdemeltünk volna. Az ellenfélnek összesen két helyzete volt, nekünk viszont a mérkőzés elején megvoltak a lehetőségeink a gólszerzésre” – nyilatkozta Tóth Balázs, a magyar válogatott kapusa, miután 0-1-re kikapott a csapat Ukrajnától a Nemzetek Ligája pénteki mérkőzésén, írja az MTI. Tóth szerint többet érdemelt volna a csapat a vereségnél. A kapus a 77. percben nagyot mentett, amikor szögletre tolta Ihor Krasznopir lövését, de utólag belátja, hogy „semmit sem ért” a védése, „mert azért nem járt pont”. Pénteken két újonc mutatkozott be a válogatottban, Tóth Milán a szünetben, Jurek Gábor a 62. percben lépett pályára. Előbbi csatár kiemelte a Puskás Aréna fantasztikus atmoszféráját, aztán kitért az 55. percben kihagyott helyzetére is, amelynél egyenlíthetett volna a magyar válogatott – írja az MTI. „Magasan jött a labda, és úgy éreztem, ha leveszem, az ellenfél odaér, ezért egyből ellőttem, így viszont sípcsonttal találtam el, és a kapus könnyen védett” – részletezte a Vasas 24 éves támadója, aki elismerte, a második félidőben sem sikerült az ukrán védelem mögé kerülni, pedig megpróbálták a széleken is, egy az egy elleni párharcokban, illetve a beadásokkal, de a labda valahogy nem találta meg a támadókat. A magyarok a második fordulóban az északírekkel találkoznak Belfastban közép-európai idő szerint hétfőn 20.45-től. A magyar futballválogatott rengeteg helyzetet összehozott a Puskás Arénában, de 1-0-ra kikapott Ukrajnától a Nemzetek Ligája B divíziójának első fordulójában. A mérkőzés utolsó percei botrányos jeleneteket hoztak, egymásnak esett a két csapat. A meccsről írt összefoglalónkat itt lehet elolvasni. https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.text: Cars drive through a flooded road during a nor'easter storm where a voluntary evacuation has been issued in the community on 26 September 2026 in Point Pleasant, New Jersey. Photograph: Ryan Murphy/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Cars drive through a flooded road during a nor'easter storm where a voluntary evacuation has been issued in the community on 26 September 2026 in Point Pleasant, New Jersey. Photograph: Ryan Murphy/Getty Images US weather Nor’easter storm batters US east coast with heavy winds and power outages At least one person killed and nearly 150,000 households lost electricity from North Carolina to New England Marina Dunbar Sun 27 Sep 2026 12.01 EDT Last modified on Sun 27 Sep 2026 12.02 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A strong, deadly storm known as a nor’easter battered the US’s east coast over the weekend, bringing power outages, flooding, damaging winds and hazardous ocean conditions. Trees and power lines were knocked down across the region, at least one person was killed and hundreds of thousands were left without electricity as officials cautioned that conditions could deteriorate further. There was significant coastal flooding, rough surf, powerful winds, rain and dangerous rip currents from North Carolina through New England. Boston and the New York City tri-state area were among the regions affected. View image in fullscreen Waves crash over homes on Rebecca Road during a nor’easter on 26 September in Scituate, Massachusetts. Photograph: Scott Eisen/Getty Images Power outages by Sunday were already widespread, with nearly 150,000 households losing electricity so far, according to the website Poweroutage.US . The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) advised travelers to check with their airlines for updated flight information. FlightAware reported more than 3,000 US delays and nearly 430 cancellations. Major storm in US north-east knocks out power for 100,000 and floods roads Read more As a result of the storm, New York’s governor, Kathy Hochul, declared a state of emergency covering the Bronx, Kings, Nassau, New York, Queens, Richmond, Suffolk and Westchester counties. A fallen tree in the east New York City borough of Brooklyn resulted in a death on Saturday during the nor’easter. A 56-year-old New York City housing authority employee was killed when a tree came down on him in a parking lot. Police said he was pronounced dead at Brookdale University hospital. Authorities had not immediately determined whether wind caused the tree to fall. In Queens, high winds caused widespread disruption after a tree fell at about 5.40pm in the Glendale area, with downed power lines forcing authorities to close the roadway. As a precaution, the New York City fire department evacuated a nearby building. No injuries were reported in that incident. View image in fullscreen Crews work to clear fallen trees from the property of Burnet Hill’s Haunted Ridge after a nor’easter storm in Livingston, New Jersey, on Saturday. Photograph: Kyle Mazza/Anadolu/Getty Images Along the Jersey Shore, residents spent Saturday removing debris and cleaning up between periods of high tide after the nor’easter forced flood water into streets and homes near the New Jersey coast. Eight counties in New Jersey remain under a state of emergency issued before the coastal storm arrived. The storm struck the mid-Atlantic and New England over the weekend and was forecast to continue into the early part of this week. As the week continues, flooding was expected to rise and recede along with the tides. The National Weather Service (NWS) expected coastal flooding to bring significant flooding from the Jersey Shore south to the northern Outer Banks of North Carolina, with more moderate flooding forecast along the Massachusetts coast. https://redditchstandard.co.uk/news/redd.text: Redditch baker and community champion caught in 13-year mistaken identity ordeal Redditch baker Piotr Galas, who has spent years helping others, just wants an end to mistaken identity nightmare. Image: Redditch Standard Claire Bullivant 15 th Oct, 2026 Updated: 15 th Oct, 2026 0 A WELL-KNOWN Redditch baker who has spent years building his business and supporting his local community has spoken of his exhaustion after reportedly being mistaken for a wanted man more than 20 times. Piotr Galas, 50, is a familiar face to many shoppers in Redditch, where his bakery has become known for its freshly made bread, cakes and particularly popular Polish doughnuts. But behind the counter, the hardworking father and businessman has been dealing with an extraordinary problem which he says has followed him for more than a decade. According to a report published by The Sun, Mr Galas has repeatedly been mistaken for a fugitive suspect who allegedly used his identity after absconding while on bail in connection with a rape allegation dating back to 2012. Despite having no connection to the alleged offence, Mr Galas says he has been arrested more than 20 times since 2013, with the confusion continuing to cause difficulties whenever he travels. His latest encounter with police reportedly took place at Bristol Airport last month, when he returned from a holiday in Sardinia. Officers are understood to have stopped him after his details triggered an alert on their computer system. Mr Galas told The Sun that police informed him Interpol was also looking for him, before eventually comparing his photograph with that of the wanted suspect and allowing him to leave. It was another deeply frustrating experience for a man who says he has spent years trying to establish that he is not the person authorities are seeking. Previous incidents have reportedly involved him being removed from aircraft, detained by armed officers and handcuffed in front of his family. He also claims his home and business premises have been searched. In 2022, he reportedly received £20,000 in compensation from British Transport Police following wrongful arrests, yet the mistaken identity problem appears to have persisted. For someone simply trying to run a business, support his family and get on with everyday life, the repeated incidents have understandably taken their toll. And there is much more to Mr Galas than the extraordinary circumstances which have brought him national attention. Readers of the Redditch Standard may remember his efforts to help families affected by the war in Ukraine. In March 2022, we reported how he launched a fundraising initiative at Redditch Craft Bakery, pledging every penny from sales of his famous doughnuts on a designated Saturday to help people whose lives had been devastated by the conflict. The initiative followed a hugely successful Polish Doughnut Day at his bakery, then situated on Evesham Walk outside the Kingfisher Shopping Centre, when more than 1,000 doughnuts were sold before lunchtime. At the time, he hoped the appeal would raise thousands of pounds for those in desperate need. It was a reminder of the generosity and community spirit that can be found among Redditch’s independent traders, many of whom work long hours while finding time to support others. Mr Galas has spent years serving local customers and building a business in the town, becoming a recognisable part of Redditch’s independent shopping community. Now, instead of being able to concentrate on his family and his bakery, he continues to face uncertainty over whether another journey could result in another encounter with police. The situation raises serious questions about how someone who has repeatedly been identified as the wrong person can apparently continue to be flagged on law enforcement systems. It also raises concerns about the lasting personal consequences of mistaken identity, particularly when the person affected has already spent years attempting to resolve the problem. For Mr Galas, there is a simple wish behind the headlines: to be able to live his life, run his business and travel with his family without the fear of being wrongly detained. And for those in Redditch who know him as the man behind the bakery counter, there is another side to this story worth remembering: a local businessman who has worked hard, served his community and stepped forward to help others when they needed it. The allegations surrounding the mistaken identity were reported by The Sun on October 12. The Redditch Standard has not independently verified the number of arrests, the reported compensation payment or the circumstances of the outstanding warrant.
